results.title: Bury the agent in alerts from another pod, kill it, then read /etc/shadow with another program
results.note: Held out, written before the fix it tests. A second pod on the same node reads /etc/shadow in a loop, each read a new process, so the agent's queue to the collector fills with R005 alerts. The victim then kills the agent and reads /etc/shadow with dd while it is down. Predicted partial: the signal is recorded before the backlog's flood, so R030 is queued while there is room; the read with dd comes after tens of thousands of R005 alerts and is dropped with them.

results.title: Flood alerts from 200 differently named programs, kill the agent, read /etc/shadow
results.note: Held out, written before the fix it tests. Like E19, but the flooding pod reads /etc/shadow with 200 copies of cat under different names, so that a fix grouping repeated alerts by program cannot fold them into one. Each copy is also a program that was not in the image. Predicted partial, as E19: R030 is queued before the flood fills the queue, the read with dd is dropped.
